question: Will the Fed Pause-Hike-Pause in the next three decisions (Oct-Dec-Jan)?
rules:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds rate. The decisions on the target federal funds rate are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: October 27 to 28; December 8 to 9; and January 26 to 27.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other". Any rate cut will be encompassed by "Other".

Emergency rate changes outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

question: Russian missile or drone impact in an EU country by December 15, 2026?
rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a qualifying Russian munition impacts the territory of an EU member state between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A qualifying munition is a missile (including cruise, ballistic, and air-to-surface missiles) or an uncrewed aerial vehicle launched by the armed forces of Russia, including attack, decoy, and reconnaissance drones (e.g., Shahed/Geran, Gerbera, Orlan), regardless of its size, range, or whether it carries a warhead or explosive payload. Munitions launched by private military contractors, mercenaries, proxy forces, or the armed forces of any other state, including Belarus, will not qualify.

A qualifying munition impacts an EU member state if it crashes, strikes the ground, or detonates on or over the territory of that state without having been intercepted. The intended target is irrelevant: a munition that enters an EU member state in the course of a Russian attack on Ukraine or any other country, including due to malfunction or navigational error, will qualify.

A munition brought down by air defenses or electronic warfare of any party, including jamming or spoofing, or that crashes after being hit by air defenses, will be considered intercepted. This includes a munition diverted off course by jamming or spoofing that later crashes or detonates on the territory of an EU member state. A navigational error caused by electronic warfare does not qualify as navigational error under this market.

The following will not qualify: munitions intercepted or destroyed by air defenses before impact, and any debris, fragments, or wreckage from intercepted munitions, regardless of any damage incurred; airspace violations by munitions that leave the territory without impacting it; surface-to-air missiles; artillery, rocket artillery, and mortars; and ATGMs.

An "EU member state" refers to any of the 27 member states of the European Union as of market creation: Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, and Sweden.

The territory of an EU member state refers to its terrestrial territory, including its internal waters. Maritime territory and airspace are not encompassed. Territories of member states to which the EU treaties do not apply, including Greenland, the Faroe Islands, and the overseas countries and territories associated with the EU, will not qualify. Where territorial borders are disputed, all territory claimed by and under the de facto control of the EU member state as of market creation will qualify.

The occurrence, attribution, and timing of a qualifying impact will be primarily determined based on a consensus of information available from the resolution sources. No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by the totality of information.

Unless a qualifying impact has already been established by a consensus of information available from the resolution sources, this market will remain open until 11:59 PM ET on the third calendar date following the specified date. If multiple sources conflict regarding the occurrence, attribution, or timing of a potentially-qualifying incident at 11:59 PM ET on the third calendar date following the specified date, the incident will be adjudicated based on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments and militaries of Russia and the relevant EU member state, official information from NATO and the European Union, and a consensus of credible reporting.
